rationale: Both correctly land approve_with_nits on a well-scoped, verified-correct fix (making <arg_value> optional; blast radius confined to glm47_moe.py, 17 tests pass) with zero noise and zero false positives. Review 1 caught the most consequential behavioral change: making the partial regex match an empty value streams an unterminated `{"city": "` on truncation right after </arg_key>, invalid JSON one token earlier than before; I reproduced this exactly via a streaming experiment, and it honestly bounds the impact as a small widening of a pre-existing window, plus a grounded AGENTS.md model-eval nit. Review 2's sole finding (leading-whitespace asymmetry on the recovery path) is also real and I reproduced it ('  Beijing  ' preserved vs 'x  ' when the tag is dropped), but it is an even lower-impact, self-acknowledged accepted-behavior nit. Review 1 wins on depth of verification and the higher-value catch.
notes: I independently reproduced both reviews' findings with the provided venv. Review 1's minor finding is genuine: truncation after </arg_key> -> '{"city": "' (INVALID_JSON), well-formed and missing-open-tag full inputs -> '{"city": "Beijing"}'. One small imprecision in Review 1's supporting detail: it states the pre-change regex 'produced {}' on this truncation, whereas monkeypatching the old (mandatory <arg_value>) regexes yields empty streamed args ('') not '{}'; either way the pre-change path was not invalid mid-string, so the regression direction/claim stands and I did not treat it as a false positive. Review 2 correctly reported HEAD 9dee6db1bbce... which matches the checkout. Both reviews' claims that the file test suite passes (17) and that the regexes/converter are used only in glm47_moe.py are confirmed.
